message.content:
Implement 5 fixes in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (Nxeon migration engine, Docker/compose/image bring-up). Edit only that file. After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` (green). Do NOT run the worker, deploy, or commit. Read the relevant regions first. Report final line numbers per fix. Keep every existing honest gate intact; when unsure, refuse-and-name rather than proceed.

Context: `ensureImage` (~1705) returns `{status:"present"|"pulled"|"loaded"|"failed",detail}` and confirms success with `docker image inspect <ref>`. The compose bring-up loop uses `composeEnvFor` → `ce.fileArg`/`ce.composeFiles`/`ce.args`, a per-project `projArg` (-p), an external-NETWORK pre-pass, a compose image pre-flight (`config --images` → ensureImage), and an N-of-M verdict. `BUILTIN_NETWORKS` (Set) exists ~352; there's a network-name validator used by the net pre-pass — reuse its pattern for volumes.

## FIX IMG-1 — digest-pinned images: confirm by image ID, not by @sha256 (HIGH — a successful transfer is reported as failed)
`docker load` does NOT restore RepoDigests, so after a successful `docker save|load` of a `repo@sha256:…` ref, `docker image inspect <ref>` returns non-zero and `ensureImage` wrongly returns `failed`, blocking compose. In `ensureImage` (~1705-1749): when the ref contains `@sha256:`, confirm presence a different way. Options that work: the save/load stream can `docker load` and you then verify via `docker image inspect` on the ref WITHOUT the digest is not possible (no tag), so instead: after `docker load`, parse the loaded image ID from `docker load`'s output ("Loaded image ID: sha256:…" or "Loaded image: …") and confirm with `docker image inspect <thatID>`; OR before deciding failed, check `docker image inspect <ref>` AND, if that fails but the ref is digest-pinned, check whether ANY local image has that repo digest via `docker images --digests --format '{{.Repository}}@{{.Digest}}'` matching the ref. Implement the most robust of these. Net effect: a digest-pinned image that was actually loaded is reported `loaded`, not `failed`. Preserve the existing tag-based confirm for non-digest refs.

## FIX IMG-2 — architecture/platform mismatch: honest-refuse instead of shipping a non-runnable image (HIGH)
The engine `save/load`s an arm64 image onto an amd64 target and reports success; it fails later as `exec format error`. Capture the TARGET arch once (`docker version -f '{{.Server.Arch}}'` or `uname -m` normalized) and the source image's arch. For an image being transferred, read its arch on the SOURCE (`${onSource(\`docker image inspect -f '{{.Architecture}}' <ref>\`)}`) OR after load read `docker image inspect -f '{{.Architecture}}' <ref>` on target; if it mismatches the target arch (amd64/x86_64 vs arm64/aarch64), do NOT count it success — push/return a clear refuse naming both arches ("the old server's image <ref> is <srcArch>; this server is <tgtArch> — it must be rebuilt or repulled for <tgtArch>"). Wire it so the compose pre-flight and the standalone image step both surface it as a failed/blocked step rather than a green image that won't run. Keep it cheap; don't block on unknown arch (only refuse on a definite mismatch).

## FIX VOL-1 — external named VOLUMES pre-pass (mirror the external-network one) (HIGH)
There is a pre-pass that creates genuinely-orphan external NETWORKS before bring-up; there is NO equivalent for `volumes: { x: { external: true } }`, so a stack referencing a shared external volume aborts with `volume "x" declared as external, but could not be found`. Add a volume pre-pass right beside the network one: across all `plan.composeDirs`, parse each project's top-level `volumes:` block (same awk approach the network pre-pass uses on `networks:`), classify `external: true` (name = `name:` override else `<project>_<key>`? — NO: for volumes an external's real name is the `name:` override else the KEY itself, exactly like networks) vs project-owned (`<project>_<key>`). For each external NOT owned by a migrated project and matching the name validator, `docker volume inspect <v> >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker volume create <v>`. IMPORTANT interaction with data-safety: if that external volume SHOULD hold data (it's in the copied set) it's filled by the volume copy loop; a genuinely-unowned empty external just needs to exist. Do not create a volume a migrated project owns. Best-effort try/catch; never block bring-up.

## FIX CMP-1 — compose v1→v2 image-name mismatch for build:-only services (HIGH)
For a service with `build:` and no `image:`, `docker compose config --images` on the v2 target synthesizes `project-service`, but the source (if it ran compose v1) tagged the built image `project_service` — so the pre-flight's `ensureImage` tries `docker save project-service` on the source, which lacks that tag, and wrongly refuses a healthy build stack. Fix in the compose image pre-flight: when `ensureImage` fails for a ref that looks compose-synthesized (contains the project name + service), before declaring a block, retry with the `_`↔`-` variant of the ref (try `project_service` if `project-service` failed and vice-versa). Better: resolve the built image from the SOURCE's actual running container image (`c.image` from the inspect for a container in this project) when available, rather than the target-synthesized name. Implement the `_`↔`-` fallback at minimum so a v1-source build stack transfers.

## FIX PROF-1 — profiles: inactive-service ${VAR} causes false "missing settings" refuse (MED-HIGH)
The required-var scan greps `${VAR}` across all compose files with no profile awareness, so a var only a `profiles:`-gated (inactive) service needs is flagged missing → the whole project is refused. Change the required-var derivation to use `docker compose ${fileArg}${args}${projArg} config` (which drops inactive-profile services and resolves interpolation) and scan ITS output for unresolved/required vars, instead of raw-grepping the files — OR intersect the grep results with the services that `config --services` reports as active. Keep the refuse behavior for genuinely-missing active-service vars.

## Constraints
- Reuse existing helpers/validators; match the single-quoted `sh -c '…'` style; validate any interpolated name.
- Each fix must be surgical and within the bring-up/image region. Do not regress the data-safety guards (F2 projArg, F3 empty-volume, A1) added just before you.
- Finish only when tsc is clean and the test passes. Report per-fix final line numbers + how you confirmed digest images (IMG-1) and detected arch (IMG-2).
